title: Good curve models near a generic point
statement:
Let $S$ be a scheme and $f:X	o S$ a separated morphism of finite presentation [def-pc-scheme] [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. Let $\eta$ be the generic point of an irreducible component of $S$ [def-weil-irreducible-components] [def-sc-generic-point], and assume $\dim X_\eta\leq1$ [def-pc-scheme-fibre] [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. There exist an open neighbourhood $U\subset S$ of $\eta$, a finite surjective universally injective morphism $V	o U$, a finite family of finite etale morphisms $T_i	o V$, and commutative diagrams over $V$ $$\coprod_iY_i\xrightarrow{
u}X_V:=X	imes_SV,\qquad Y_i\xrightarrow{j_i}\overline Y_i	o T_i	o V$$ [def-pc-fibre-product] [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-coproduct-family] [def-weil-pbc-finite-etale-category], with the following properties. The map $
u$ is finite and surjective; each $j_i$ is an open immersion; $Y_i	o T_i$ is smooth and surjective; $\overline Y_i	o T_i$ is smooth and proper with geometrically connected fibres of dimension at most one [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible]. There is an open $W\subset X_V$ dense in every fibre of $X_V	o V$ such that $W_i:=
u^{-1}(W)\cap Y_i$ is dense in every fibre of $Y_i	o T_i$, and $
u^{-1}(W)	o W$ is a thickening, meaning a closed immersion surjective on underlying points [def-sbc-first-order-thickening]. The finite family may be empty.

proof.text: Choose an affine neighbourhood of $\eta$ and replace it by its reduction $\operatorname{Spec}A$. Its map to the original neighbourhood is a surjective closed immersion, hence finite and universally injective; it will be included in the eventual map $V\to U$. The point $\eta$ corresponds to a minimal prime $\mathfrak p$ of the reduced ring $A$, and $A_{\mathfrak p}=\kappa(\mathfrak p)=k$. Base changing $f$ keeps its separated finite-presentation hypotheses: affine-local finite-presentation base change is the cited ring lemma; the diagonal and the finite affine covers base change. The geometric generic fibre is unchanged by reduction of the base.

Apply the field completion lemma to $X_\eta/k$, obtaining $k'/k$, the normalization components $Y_{i,\eta}$, their dense open immersions into smooth projective geometrically irreducible $\overline Y_{i,\eta}$, and finite separable constant fields $k_i/k'$. A projective morphism is proper. Restriction to the dense open makes $Y_{i,\eta}\to\operatorname{Spec}k_i$ smooth, and its nonemptiness makes it surjective. If the family is empty the generic fibre is empty; the descent argument below still applies to the empty scheme.

Realize $k'/k$ on a finite radicial base cover, using a finite tower of degree-$p$ extensions: induct on $[k'/k]$, apply the intermediate-field lemma to write $k'=M(z)$ with $[k':M]=p$, construct the tower for the smaller extension $M/k$, and append $M(z)/M$; in characteristic zero the tower is empty. At a stage with reduced affine base $\operatorname{Spec}B$ and generic residue field $l$, first shrink to make $p=0$ in $B$, since $p=0$ in $B_{\mathfrak q}=l$. For the next generator $\beta$ with $\beta^p=a\in l$, shrink again to represent $a$ in $B$, and put $C=B[t]/(t^p-a)$. This is finite free on $1,t,\ldots,t^{p-1}$. Every field-valued point lifts after adjoining a root of $t^p-a$, and two roots in any field are equal because $(u-v)^p=0$. Thus $\operatorname{Spec}C\to\operatorname{Spec}B$ is surjective and universally injective by the field-point criterion. At $\mathfrak q$, $C\otimes_B l=l(\beta)$, a field, so the unique point above $\mathfrak q$ has that local ring. Reducing $C$ preserves this local field and gives another finite radicial surjection. Induct on the tower length; its terminal residue field is $k'$.

All shrinkings on an intermediate finite radicial cover can be effected by shrinking the original base: if $h:Z\to U$ is that cover and $O\subset Z$ contains the unique point over $\eta$, remove the closed set $h(Z\setminus O)$ from $U$. Choose a principal open neighbourhood of $\eta$ inside that remaining open of the original affine base. Its inverse image is contained in $O$ and is affine by finiteness of $h$. Thus both the original base and its finite cover remain affine at each stage. Finiteness and closedness of $h$ justify this operation without a Noetherian assumption. Finite composition and base change preserve finiteness; the pointwise injectivity after every base change and surjectivity persist under composition. We now have a reduced affine base $V$ finite, surjective, universally injective over an open $U$ of the original $S$, whose generic residue field is $k'$. Any later shrinking of $V$ is handled in the same way, restricting all the diagram objects by base change. For readability call this reduced affine base $\operatorname{Spec}A$ and its generic field $k$.

Express $k=A_{\mathfrak p}$ as the filtered colimit of $A_a$ for $a\notin\mathfrak p$. The affine-transition limit of $\operatorname{Spec}A_a$ is therefore $\operatorname{Spec}k$. Apply object descent to the finitely many $Y_{i,\eta}$, $\overline Y_{i,\eta}$ and $\operatorname{Spec}k_i$, keeping $X$ as its already specified model. Apply morphism descent to their finitely many arrows, and eventual equality to the finitely many commuting triangles. A common later principal localization gives a diagram $\coprod_iY_i\to X$, $Y_i\to\overline Y_i\to T_i\to\operatorname{Spec}A$, whose generic fibre is the chosen diagram. Every object is of finite presentation over the affine base and hence qcqs. Every arrow is locally of finite presentation: on affine charts apply the cited theorem on finite presentation over a finite-type intermediate algebra.

Over the generic field $\nu$ is finite and surjective: it is the normalization of the reduction followed by the surjective closed immersion of the reduction. Use the existing normalization theorem and finite composition for this assertion. Descend finiteness and surjectivity of $\nu$, openness of each $j_i$, finite etaleness of $T_i\to V$, smoothness and surjectivity of $Y_i\to T_i$, and smoothness and properness of $\overline Y_i\to T_i$, using the respective cited descent statements. Their qcqs and local finite-presentation hypotheses were established in the preceding step; the weaker local finite-type hypotheses also hold. There are only finitely many maps, so take common refinements successively. Finiteness and surjectivity persist by their base-change lemmas, smoothness and open immersion by the eventual conclusions of the two new descent statements; etaleness is smooth relative dimension zero and is unchanged under restriction of base. Properness, defined using the diagonal and universal closedness, is likewise unchanged under base restriction.

For each $i$, $T_i$ has precisely one point $\eta_i$ above $\eta$, with residue field $k_i$. Apply local constancy of geometric component count to the proper smooth finite-presentation morphism $\overline Y_i\to T_i$. The count at $\eta_i$ is one, so there is an open neighbourhood on which all fibres are geometrically connected. Apply upper semicontinuity of proper fibre dimension to obtain an open neighbourhood on which the fibres have dimension at most one. Remove from $V$ the images under the finite maps $T_i\to V$ of the closed complements of these neighbourhoods. Those images are closed and avoid $\eta$, so this is an allowed shrinking. Thus all fibres now have both required properties. Properness plus smoothness gives finite presentation here: the objects are qcqs and smooth implies locally of finite presentation.

Apply the reduced algebraic normalization theorem to $(X_\eta)_{\mathrm{red}}$. Its dense normal open has normalization an isomorphism. View this open on $X_\eta$, whose reduction has the same underlying space. The normalization map above this open is then the inclusion of its reduction, a closed immersion surjective on points. Choose a quasi-compact dense subopen $W_\eta$ there: take finitely many affine neighbourhoods, inside that normal open, of the generic points of the finitely many components indexed by the normalization. Its inverse image meets every $Y_{i,\eta}$. By the scheme-over-limit lemma $X_\eta$ is the inverse limit of the qcqs $X_{A_a}$. Descend $W_\eta$ to a quasi-compact open $W$ at a stage using quasi-compact-open descent. The inverse image of $W$ under the finite $
u$ is also qcqs, and its map to $W$ is locally of finite type. Closed-immersion descent therefore makes $
u^{-1}(W)	o W$ a closed immersion after a further localization. It is surjective by base change of the surjective $
u$, so is a thickening, with no square-zero assertion.

Put $W_i=\nu^{-1}(W)\cap Y_i$. The map $W_i\to T_i$ is open: it is the restriction of a smooth morphism, smooth implies flat and locally of finite presentation, and such maps are open. Its image contains $\eta_i$ by construction of $W_\eta$. Since $T_i\to V$ is finite, remove from $V$ the closed images of the complements of these open images. After this shrinking every $W_i\to T_i$ is surjective. Each fibre of $\overline Y_i\to T_i$ is smooth and geometrically connected and hence geometrically irreducible: after any field extension apply the integral-geometry core with base the spectrum of that field (integral, with integrally closed local rings), smooth source the nonempty connected fibre. Its conclusion that the source is integral gives irreducibility. The nonempty open fibre of $Y_i$ is therefore irreducible too. Its nonempty open subspace $(W_i)_t$ is dense. For smoothness after a field extension $F/\kappa(t)$, take affine first-order thickening test data over $F$ and forget the $F$-structure. Formal smoothness over $\kappa(t)$ supplies a lift to the original fibre; pair it with the given map of the thickening to $\operatorname{Spec}F$ to obtain a lift to the fibre product. Local finite presentation follows on affine charts from the cited finite-presentation base-change lemma.

Fix $v\in V$ and a nonempty open in the fibre $(Y_i)_v$ of $Y_i\to V$. Choose a point in it and let $t$ be its image in $T_i$, necessarily above $v$. Intersection with the fibre $(Y_i)_t$ is a nonempty open, so meets the dense open $(W_i)_t$. Thus $(W_i)_v$ is dense in $(Y_i)_v$. Taking the finite disjoint union shows $\nu^{-1}(W)$ is dense in every fibre of $\coprod_iY_i\to V$. The map of this fibre onto $(X_V)_v$ is surjective by surjective base change. The image of a dense subset under a continuous surjection is dense: the inverse image of every nonempty open is nonempty open and meets the dense subset. Its image is exactly $W_v$ since $\nu$ is surjective. Consequently $W$ is dense in every fibre of $X_V\to V$. This proves all clauses. If $I$ is empty, the descended surjection from the empty scheme forces $X_V$ to be empty; choose $W=\varnothing$.
